title: Hartwell paid about $317K a year in vendor bill lines above PO value (2016-2025). Only about $85K a year of that is provably qty never received (stock POs). About $150K is special-order qty with no receipt record, and about $82K is unit cost that can't be judged.
conclusion: Holds with changes. Observed: over 2016-2025, 13,949 bills paid in full carried line value above their PO, 3,166,564.74 in total. That is 316,656.47 a year, or 0.2956% of 1,071,302,610.84 PO value on paid-in-full bills (q231, q126). Every year is between 272,768.64 (2023) and 429,671.84 (2016) (q231). This is a gross figure. All 1,234 vendor credits trace to vendor-return movements once they are matched on vendor_id, so no credit offsets it. My earlier 273,967.29 floor came from a join error and is withdrawn (q166, q169). The excess has three parts with different evidence. (a) Qty billed above PO on stock POs: 847,795.65 (84,779.56 a year). Every billed stock line has a WMS receipt equal to PO qty, so the billed extra was demonstrably not received (q164, q231). (b) Qty billed above PO on special-order POs: 1,498,042.39 (149,804.24 a year). Special orders have no WMS receipt at all (121,364 paid-in-full lines, 0 with a receipt), so receipt can't be checked. Indirectly, on all 1,228 of 1,290 qty-over lines that match exactly one customer sales line, the customer was shipped the PO qty and never the billed qty. That is consistent with non-delivery but doesn't prove it (q164, q193). (c) Unit cost above PO on lines without qty-over: 820,726.70 (82,072.67 a year). Whether this was owed can't be judged: PO cost equals the product master cost on every line and never changed for any of 1,096 SKUs in ten years, so the PO isn't an independent price reference (q171, q183, q231). Interpretation: AP paid exactly PO value, excluding freight, on about 30% of bills that differed from the PO for any reason, including freight-only bills (0.3008), and on 0 of 322,260 bills that matched. That looks like a pay-to-PO rule applied to a fraction of variance bills, not a three-way match (q197, q202). Action: hold any bill line whose qty exceeds the receipt (or, for special orders, the customer shipment) or whose unit cost exceeds the PO. Claim (a) against receipts first. Claim (b) with vendor proof of delivery. Start with 2024-2025: 658,006.40 in total, of which (a) is 157,039.15.

claims.text: Bills reconcile: all 368,154 bills equal line value plus freight, and paid-in-full bills were paid that amount. Bill lines join to PO lines on po_id+sku. No line bills less qty or less unit cost than the PO. Paid-in-full excess is 3,166,564.74 on 1,071,302,610.84 of PO value (0.2956%), 2016-2025.
Excess is a level, not a spike: 272,768.64 (2023) to 429,671.84 (2016) a year. Without each year's top 10 lines, every year stays at 250,088.62 or more. The largest single line is 3,219.00.

Stock-PO qty-over (proven unreceived): every billed stock line has a receipt equal to PO qty (446,852 of 446,852 paid-in-full lines). Qty-over excess on stock POs is 847,795.65, or 84,779.56 a year; 157,039.15 of it falls in 2024-2025.

Special-order qty-over (not provable from receipts): 121,364 paid-in-full special-order lines have no WMS receipt. Their qty-over excess is 1,498,042.39 (149,804.24 a year). Of 1,290 qty-over lines, 1,228 (0.9519) match exactly one special sales line. On all 1,228 the customer was shipped the PO qty, and on 0 was the customer shipped the billed qty or more. The other 62 match several sales lines and are ambiguous.

Unit-cost excess without qty-over is 820,726.70 (82,072.67 a year). PO unit cost never varies for any of 1,096 SKUs and equals the product master cost on all 568,216 paid-in-full lines, so whether these costs were owed can't be tested. After the first overpriced line for a vendor-SKU, later lines are overpriced at 0.0249, the same as the base share. This argues against a general price increase, but it is weak evidence given the static PO prices.

Vendor credits don't offset the excess: all 1,234 credits (all from OEM vendors 1-4) match a return_vendor movement on vendor_id+sku+qty within 60 days. The earlier 'unmatched 426,891.88' came from joining return ref_id (a vendor id) to PO ids.

Short-pay pattern: all 12,026 short-paid bills were paid exactly PO value, with freight excluded. The short-pay share is 0.3008 on freight-only variance bills (6,115 of 20,329), 0.2986 on line-excess bills without freight (5,566 of 18,639), 0.2826 with both (345 of 1,221), and 0.0 on 322,260 matching bills. The caught share of overbilled bills is 0.2755-0.3122 in every year (overall 0.2976, 5,911 of 19,860).

confidence: high for the amount paid above PO and for the stock-PO qty-over part; medium for special-order qty-over; low for whether the unit-cost part was owed
not_evidence_of: Not evidence that any vendor or any AP staff member acted in bad faith. The pattern is uniform across 44 vendors and ten years, and its very regular structure (narrow ratio band, mostly +1 unit, flat rates, PO prices that never change) may partly reflect how the records were produced. Not evidence that special-order units were never delivered, since no receipt record exists for special orders. Not evidence that the higher unit costs were wrong: there are no price lists or contracts. Not evidence that purchasing costs are generally inflated (0.2956% of PO value). Not evidence that AP's short-pays were correct: some withheld freight may have been owed.
could_not_tell: Whether special-order units above PO qty were delivered (needs vendor proof of delivery or a special-order receiving record). Whether the higher unit costs were contractually valid (needs vendor price lists or contracts; PO cost is a fixed master price). What freight was owed (no freight terms). How AP picked the bills it short-paid (no approval or dispute history). Whether any excess was disputed or credited outside these tables. The vendor dispute window, which decides how much of 2016-2023 is recoverable.
next_step: Put a match hold on bill lines where qty exceeds the receipt (stock) or the customer shipment (special), or where unit cost exceeds the PO. Pull the paid-in-full stock-PO qty-over lines and claim them against receipts, starting with 2024-2025 (157,039.15). Ask OEM vendors for proof of delivery on special-order qty-over lines. Get vendor price agreements before pursuing unit-cost differences. Ask AP how short-pay bills are chosen and whether freight withheld on freight-only bills was owed. Separately, review the 963 paid second bills on duplicate-billed POs (2,732,286.38, q172).
dead_ends: Vendor credits as offset: all 1,234 credits are vendor-return credits once correctly matched (q169); the earlier unmatched-credit floor was a join error
Price-step test: no step per vendor-SKU (q110), but uninformative because PO cost never changes (q183)
Outlier or single-year drive: none; every year at 250,088.62 or more without its top 10 lines (q205)
Short-paid vs paid-in-full bills differing systematically: no; short-pay share is about 30% for any variance, including freight-only (q202)
response_to_challenge: I accepted every point, re-ran the sizing in one query (q231), and did the arithmetic for the recent years in q234. (1) Receipt claim: accepted. 'Receipts always equal PO qty' holds only for stock POs. Special orders have no receipt record (q164). I split the qty-over excess into a proven stock part (847,795.65; 84,779.56 a year) and an unproven special-order part (1,498,042.39; 149,804.24 a year), and I cite the challenger's indirect customer-shipment test (q193) as supporting but not proving evidence. (2) Credit test: accepted. My q117 joined return_vendor ref_id (a vendor id) to PO ids. Correctly matched, all 1,234 credits trace to returns (q169), so I dropped the 273,967.29 floor and the figure is gross. (3) Price-step argument: accepted as weak. PO cost is a static master price (q171, q183), so the cost part (82,072.67 a year) is now 'can't judge'. (4) Short-pay selection: accepted. AP pays PO value excluding freight on about 30% of any variance bill (q197, q202), so I removed the claim that AP 'catches' overbills and added the freight question. (5) Outliers: the challenge confirmed the level (q205); no change. (6) Recoverability: accepted. The action now starts with 2024-2025 (658,006.40 in total; 157,039.15 of it proven stock qty-over, q187, q234). I kept dollars_a_year as the ten-year average paid above PO value (316,656.47, q231), because that amount is an observed payment whatever its cause. I lowered confidence on the parts that can't be proven, and the title now states the proven 84,779.56-a-year portion separately. The 84,779.56 here and the 84,779.57 in q207 differ only by rounding. The duplicate-bill issue is noted as separate, not added to this finding.
